text.p: DeKalb Genetics Corp, a seed company, said Thursday it continues to be comfortable with analysts' estimates for fiscal 1997 earnings of $1.60 a share.
In fiscal 1996 ended August 31, it earned $1.03 a share.
DeKalb also said it expects strong revenue growth for the North American corn seed business and a record contribution from international seed operations.

In a statement issued from Minneapolis, where the company presented at the Piper Jaffray investors conference, DeKalb also said it expects unit margins for its North American corn seed business to exceed earlier expectations.

"We are very comfortable with a $5 or better improvement in unit margins, compared with 1996," Richard Ryan, president and chief operating officer, said in a statement. "Although some of our competitors engaged in seed promotions late in the selling season, we chose to hold firm on pricing. Our unit margins should be better than we anticipated as recently as two months ago."

DeKalb, the second largest seed corn producer behind Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc, still expects a market share gain. But it will be at the lower end of the previously targeted range of one-half to one percentage point, Ryan said.
He blamed competitive pricing actions for taking "some of the top off" DeKalb's market share gain this year.
DeKalb added that uncertainty about planted acreage and returned goods makes it too early to determine final numbers.
Sales volume of DeKalb soybean seed is projected to be up significantly, reaching a record high, the company said.
International seed operations are exceeding expectations, and the company anticipates a record contribution, led by Argentina and Mexico, it added.

"In Argentina, we had a very strong finish this year," Ryan said. "With exceptional product performance in a high-disease environment, DeKalb Argentina is positioned well for significant earnings and market share gains in 1998."
